title: SQL Databases
subtitle: An index turns a scan into a handful of page reads, and you pay for it on every write
motto: Index for the questions you ask, and only those
keyInsight: A B-tree index makes a lookup cost a few page reads regardless of table size, but every extra index slows every write and takes space.

decisions.title: Show the query that cannot use the index
decisions.description: The failure frame is an unindexable query, because the common mistake is not a missing index but a query written so the index cannot help.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only 'no index versus index' would leave learners thinking any index fixes any query.

decisions.title: Price writes, not just reads
decisions.description: The trade-off frame reports write time and storage for indexing everything, since over-indexing is the opposite failure to under-indexing.
decisions.alternatives: Reporting only query speed would make more indexes look strictly better.
